newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel flat, Russian trades strong.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel flat, Russian trades strong.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was unchanged on Tuesday with sellers at $105 and buyers at the $101/$102 mark, while high sulphur Russian material fetched a strong price, traders said.
High sulphur Russian straight-run was heard offered as high as two means plus $6 early in the day, or the $90 cif mark, and a cargo was bought later by a refiner at two means plus $5.50.
"It was good quality material out of Tallinn. Lower quality stuff from other places is on offer at two means +$5 and bids are at two means +$4," a trader with a major said.
Traders said that demand continued for straight-run from refiners who have cut runs recently with crude's gains, but with most of the cargoes snatched up, the trend my slow down in the near future.
E-4, the scarcest of the Russian straight-run, was offered $1 higher at two means plus $5, the price a cargo was heard to have traded at in the Mediterranean on Monday.
But things were quieter on the low sulphur straight-run market, traders said.

"It's another quiet day, the numbers are not different from yesterday," one trader said, adding that the 0.5-0.7 sulphur material was not affected by crude futures' move southwards overnight then gains today.
A U.S. independent refiner was re-offering a 20,000-tonne cargo picked up originally for trans-Atlantic shipment. One trader said the seller was hoping for a cif price of $108/$109 a tonne.
"It is distressed. It's a funny-sized cargo, 20,000 tonnes and that's causing the problems but may be they can find someone to take it to the States," a trader said.
A refiner was heard asking a high $112 a tonne for its 0.4 pct or less sulphur straight-run but no active buyers were heard.
